steps: In ∆AOB and ∆COD: AB = CD, ∠AOB = ∠COD (vertically opposite), and ∠ABD = ∠CDB (each is 90° minus the same angle).

Each half is 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm.

item.question: Equal diagonals bisect each other at 40°. Find the angles of the quadrilateral.
steps: In the triangle with 40° at O, the base angles add to 180 − 40 = 140, so each is 140 ÷ 2 = 70.
The next triangle has 180 − 40 = 140 at O, so its base angles add to 180 − 140 = 40, and each is 20.
Each corner of the quadrilateral is 70 + 20 = 90.
item.answer: All four angles are 90°, so it is again a rectangle

item.question: ABCD has all four angles 90°. Show that AD = CB and DC = BA, and say why writing ∆BAD ≅ ∆CDB is wrong.
steps_tex: Join the diagonal $BD$.
$\angle BAD = \angle DCB = 90^\circ$, and $BD$ is common to $\triangle BAD$ and $\triangle DCB$.
$\angle ABD + \angle DBC = 90^\circ$ and $\angle CDB + \angle DBC = 90^\circ$, so $\angle ABD = \angle CDB$.
By $AAS$, $\triangle BAD \cong \triangle DCB$, matching $B$ with $D$, $C$ with $A$ and $D$ with $B$.
So $AD = CB$ and $BA = DC$.
$\triangle CDB$ would match $D$ with $A$, but the right angle at $A$ has to match the right angle at $C$, not $D$.
item.answer_tex: $AD = CB$ and $DC = BA$; $\triangle BAD \cong \triangle CDB$ is wrong because the vertices are not in matching order

item.question: A sheet is folded in half and then into a quarter, and one slanting crease is made across the corner at the middle of the sheet. What shape do the creases make, and how should you fold to get a square?
steps: The two folds cross at right angles at the centre of the sheet.
Unfolding copies the crease into all four quarters, so the shape has four equal sides.
Its diagonals lie along the folds, so they bisect each other at right angles: a rhombus.
Several creases parallel to the first give rhombuses inside one another.
If the crease cuts off equal lengths along both folds, the diagonals are equal too, and the rhombus is a square.
item.answer: A rhombus; fold the crease at 45°, cutting equal lengths on both folds, to get a square
